title: Busy until three
goal: Tell Sēf until when you're busy, and plan to meet after your lecture
tip: lēn means 'until'. Put it before a time or a noun, lēn is-sāʿa thalāth 'until three', or before a present verb, lēn tkhalliṣ 'until you finish'. ʿugub is the Emirati 'after' before a noun: ʿugub il-muḥāẓra 'after the lecture'. baʿd works everywhere.
dialogue: A
هلا! وين كنت؟ نتغدى مع بعض اليوم؟
hala! wēn kint? nitghadda maʿa baʿaẓ il-yōm?
Hi! Where have you been? Shall we have lunch together today?
B
هلا فيك! ما أقدر، عندي شغل لين الساعة ثلاث
hala fīk! ma agdar, ʿindi shughul lēn is-sāʿa thalāth
Hi! I can't, I've got work until three.
A
عادي، نتغدى عقب الشغل
ʿādi, nitghadda ʿugub ish-shughul
No problem, we'll have lunch after work.
B
بس بعد الغدا عندي محاضرة لين ست
bas baʿd il-ghada ʿindi muḥāẓra lēn sitt
But after lunch I've got a lecture until six.
A
زين، وعقب المحاضرة؟ بترياك لين تخلص
zēn, w ʿugub il-muḥāẓra? batrayyāk lēn tkhalliṣ
OK, and after the lecture? I'll wait for you until you finish.
B
مشكور! بعد المغرب نروح المول؟
mashkūr! baʿd il-maghrib nrūḥ il-mōl?
Thanks! Shall we go to the mall after maghrib?
A
العفو. اتفقنا! من زمان ما شفتك
il-ʿafu. ittafagna! min zamān ma shiftak
You're welcome. Deal! I haven't seen you for ages!
items: also before a present verb: lēn tkhalliṣ 'until you finish'
baʿd (بعد) is the everyday form everywhere: baʿd il-maghrib
I'll wait for you (to a man) (UAE)
to a woman: lēn tkhallṣīn (لين تخلصين)
I haven't seen you for ages, long time no see (to a man)
to a woman: min zamān ma shiftich (من زمان ما شفتج)
I haven't seen you, I didn't see you (to a man)
to a woman: ma shiftich (ما شفتج)

title: After work, step by step
goal: At the office, tell Maryam what you did after work yesterday, in order
tip: To say 'after I did something', put baʿd ma before a past verb: baʿd ma khallaṣt 'after I finished'. Emiratis also say ʿugub ma: ʿugub ma rijaʿt 'after I got back'. To tell steps in order: awwal shay 'first', baʿd-ha 'after that', ākhir shay 'in the end'.
grammar: baʿd ma / ʿugub ma + past: 'after I …'
dialogue: A
صباح الخير! شو سويت أمس عقب الدوام؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr! shu sawwēt ams ʿugub id-dawām?
Good morning! What did you do yesterday after work?
B
صباح النور. بعد ما خلصت، رحت المول ويا سيف
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. baʿd ma khallaṣt, riḥt il-mōl wiyya Sēf
Good morning. After I finished, I went to the mall with Sēf.
A
والله؟ شو اشتريت؟
wallāh? shu ishtarēt?
Really? What did you buy?
B
أول شي اشتريت قميص، وبعدها تعشينا
awwal shay ishtarēt gamīṣ, w baʿd-ha tʿashshēna
First I bought a shirt, and after that we had dinner.
A
حلو! وعقب ما تعشيتوا؟
ḥilu! w ʿugub ma tʿashshētu?
Nice! And after you'd had dinner?
B
آخر شي رجعت البيت ونمت. وانتي؟
ākhir shay rijaʿt il-bēt w nimt. w inti?
In the end I went home and slept. And you?
A
أنا عقب ما رجعت البيت، نمت لين الصبح!
ana ʿugub ma rijaʿt il-bēt, nimt lēn iṣ-ṣubḥ!
Me? After I got home, I slept till morning!
items: after (before a verb: after I …, after you …)
everyone also says baʿd ma (بعد ما)
after I finished; after you finished (to a man)
to a woman: baʿd ma khallaṣti (بعد ما خلصتي)
in the end, finally; the last thing
you had dinner (to a group): tʿashshētu (تعشيتوا)
I went home, I got home; you went home (to a man)

title: Before you go, have a coffee
goal: At Sēf's house, with Sēf there, leave politely at the end of the visit when Umm Sēf asks you to stay
tip: 'Before' + a verb is gabil la, and the verb after it is in the present form: gabil la trūḥ 'before you go', gabil la ansa 'before I forget'. Before a noun it's just gabil: gabil il-maghrib 'before maghrib'.
dialogue: A
وين رايح؟ اقعد لين يرجع بو سيف
wēn rāyiḥ? igʿid lēn yirjaʿ Bū Sēf
Where are you off to? Stay until Sēf's dad gets back.
B
عن إذنكم يا أم سيف، أحسن أروح. عندي محاضرة الصبح
ʿan idhnakum yā Umm Sēf, aḥsan arūḥ. ʿindi muḥāẓra ṣ-ṣubḥ
Excuse me, Umm Sēf, I'd better go. I've got a lecture in the morning.
A
زين، بس قبل لا تروح، اشرب قهوة
zēn, bas gabil la trūḥ, ishrab gahwa
All right, but before you go, have a coffee.
B
تسلمين! بشربها بسرعة قبل لا أتأخر
tislamīn! bashrabha b-surʿa gabil la atʼakhkhar
Thank you! I'll drink it quickly, before I stay too late.
A
الله يسلمك. وقبل لا أنسى، هذي حلويات حقك
allāh ysallmak. w gabil la ansa, hādhi ḥalawiyyāt ḥaggak
God keep you. And before I forget, these sweets are for you.
B
ما قصرتي! ما في داعي
mā gaṣṣarti! ma fī dāʿi
That's so kind of you! There's no need.
A
ما سوينا شي. البيت بيتك
mā sawwēna shay. il-bēt bētak
It was nothing. This is your home too.
items: to a woman: gabil la trūḥīn (قبل لا تروحين)
when leaving a host, start with ʿan idhnakum (عن إذنكم) 'excuse me (to the family)'
to a woman: ishrabi gahwa (اشربي قهوة)
to a man: tislam (تسلم); the reply is allāh ysallmak (to a man) or allāh ysallmich (to a woman)
you're always welcome here (lit. the house is your house) (to a man)
where are you off to? (to a man)
until she gets back: lēn tirjaʿ (لين ترجع)

title: As soon as I arrived
goal: Tell Sēf about the day you first came to Dubai, and about your trip to London tomorrow
tip: awwal ma means 'as soon as': awwal ma ṭilaʿt 'as soon as I came out'. With a present verb it points ahead: awwal ma tōṣal 'as soon as you get there'. yōm + a past verb means 'when': yōm wiṣalt 'when I arrived'. lamma works too.
grammar: awwal ma 'as soon as'; yōm + past 'when'
dialogue: A
شو سويت يوم ييت دبي أول مرة؟
shu sawwēt yōm yīt Dbayy awwal marra?
What did you do when you first came to Dubai?
B
يوم وصلت، كان الحر وايد!
yōm wiṣalt, kān il-ḥarr wāyid!
When I arrived, it was so hot!
A
والله؟ ولما طلعت من المطار؟
wallāh? w lamma ṭilaʿt min il-maṭār?
Really? And when you came out of the airport?
B
أول ما طلعت، شربت ماي بارد. كان أحسن شي!
awwal ma ṭilaʿt, shirabt māy bārid. kān aḥsan shay!
As soon as I came out, I drank cold water. It was the best thing ever!
A
وباكر مسافر لندن؟
w bāchir msāfir Landan?
And you're flying to London tomorrow?
B
هيه، بس قبل لا أروح لازم أخلص شغلي
hē, bas gabil la arūḥ lāzim akhalliṣ shughli
Yes, but before I go I have to finish my work.
A
زين. أول ما توصل، طرش لي رسالة
zēn. awwal ma tōṣal, ṭarrish-li risāla
OK. As soon as you land, send me a message.
items: as soon as I came out; as soon as you came out (to a man)
to a woman: awwal ma ṭilaʿti (أول ما طلعتي)
as soon as you get there (to a man)
to a woman: awwal ma tōṣlīn (أول ما توصلين)
when I arrived; when you arrived (to a man)
when I came; when you came (to a man)
to a woman: yōm yīti; you'll see written يوم جيت
lamma ṭilaʿt = yōm ṭilaʿt 'when I came out'

title: So that we're not late
goal: Get your friends to leave early for the cinema, and say what for
tip: ʿashān + a present verb means 'so that': ʿashān nilḥag 'so we make it in time'. 'So that … not' is ʿashān ma: ʿashān ma nitʼakhkhar 'so we're not late'. ʿashān shu? asks 'what for?', and ʿashān chī means 'that's why'.
dialogue: B
يا شباب، نطلع الساعة خمس عشان نلحق
yā shabāb, niṭlaʿ is-sāʿa khams ʿashān nilḥag
Guys, let's leave at five so we make it in time.
A
خمس؟ عشان شو؟ الفلم الساعة ثمان!
khams? ʿashān shu? il-film is-sāʿa thamān!
Five? What for? The film's at eight!
B
عشان نلقى باركن. وبعدها نتعشى مع بعض
ʿashān nilga bārkin. w baʿd-ha nitʿashsha maʿa baʿaẓ
So we find a parking space. And then we'll have dinner together.
A
زين، والتذاكر؟
zēn, w it-tadhākir?
OK, and the tickets?
B
اشتريتها أمس. بس تعالوا بدري عشان ما نتأخر!
ishtarēt-ha ams. bas taʿālu badri ʿashān ma nitʼakhkhar!
I bought them yesterday. Just come early so we're not late!
A
ومنو بيسوق؟
w minu biysūg?
And who's driving?
B
أنا بسوق. عشان جي قلت لكم: الساعة خمس!
ana basūg. ʿashān chī gilt-lkum: is-sāʿa khams!
I'll drive. That's why I told you: five o'clock!
items: wider Gulf and Kuwait: ʿashān chidhi (عشان جذي)
to one man: gilt-lak; to one woman: gilt-lich
so that we make it (in time)
nilḥag = we catch, we make it

title: The guy by the door
goal: Point out people and things around the university to Sēf
tip: illi 'who, that, which' never changes. Use it after a definite noun (with il- or an ending like -i 'my'): ir-rayyāl illi yamm il-bāb 'the man by the door', rbīʿi illi min Landan 'my friend from London'. Otherwise leave it out: ʿindi rbīʿ yidris hni 'I've got a friend who studies here'.
dialogue: A
منو الريّال اللي يم الباب؟
minu r-rayyāl illi yamm il-bāb?
Who's the guy by the door?
B
هذا مارك، ربيعي اللي من لندن
hādha Mārk, rbīʿi illi min Landan
That's Mark, my friend from London.
A
والشباب اللي هناك؟ أول مرة أشوفهم
w ish-shabāb illi hnāk? awwal marra ashūfhum
And the guys over there? It's the first time I've seen them.
B
هذيلا الطلاب اللي يدرسون وياي هندسة
hādhēla ṭ-ṭullāb illi yidrisūn wiyyāy handasa
They're the students who study engineering with me.
A
زين. والكتاب اللي على الطاولة، حقك؟
zēn. w il-kitāb illi ʿala ṭ-ṭāwla, ḥaggak?
OK. And the book on the table, is it yours?
B
لا، حق الطالب اللي يقعد يمي
la, ḥagg iṭ-ṭālib illi yigʿid yammi
No, it belongs to the student who sits next to me.
A
يلا، قبل لا نتأخر! المحاضرة اللي الساعة عشر بتبدا
yalla, gabil la nitʼakhkhar! il-muḥāẓra illi s-sāʿa ʿashr bitibda
Come on, before we're late! The ten o'clock lecture is about to start.
items: who, that, which (after a definite noun)
never changes for gender or number; not used after an indefinite noun; you'll see written الي
the man who, the guy who
the guys who, the young men who
it's going to start, it'll start (a feminine thing: a lecture, a party)
a masculine thing (a film, a meeting): biyibda (بيبدا)
next to you: yammak (to a man), yammich (to a woman)
my friend who, my friend (the one) …
my friend (a woman): rbīʿti illi (ربيعتي اللي)
by the door, next to the door

title: The module I'm doing now
goal: Tell Fahad about your studies, your module and your next exam
tip: illi also joins a noun to a phrase with no verb: il-māda illi ʿindi l-ḥīn 'the module I've got now', il-imtiḥān illi yōm il-ithnēn 'the exam on Monday'. dirāsa is 'studying, studies': shlōn id-dirāsa? 'how are your studies going?'
grammar: illi + a phrase with no verb
dialogue: A
شلونك؟ شلون الدراسة؟
shlōnak? shlōn id-dirāsa?
How are you? How are your studies going?
B
زين الحمد لله، بس وايد صعبة
zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh, bas wāyid ṣaʿba
Fine, thank God, but it's really hard.
A
ليش؟ شنو تخصصك؟
lēsh? shinu takhaṣṣuṣak?
Why? What's your major?
B
هندسة. والمادة اللي عندي الحين صعبة
handasa. w il-māda illi ʿindi l-ḥīn ṣaʿba
Engineering. And the module I've got now is hard.
A
عندك امتحان هالأسبوع؟
ʿindak imtiḥān hal-usbūʿ?
Have you got an exam this week?
B
هيه، الامتحان اللي يوم الاثنين. بدرس لين الليل
hē, il-imtiḥān illi yōm il-ithnēn. badris lēn il-lēl
Yes, the one on Monday. I'll study until late at night.
A
إن شاء الله تنجح! وبعد الامتحان نطلع مع بعض
in shāʼ allāh tinjaḥ! w baʿd il-imtiḥān niṭlaʿ maʿa baʿaẓ
I hope you pass! And after the exam let's go out together.
items: your major, your subject (at university) (to a man)
the exam that, the exam (which is) …
I hope you pass (to a man)
to a woman: in shāʼ allāh tinjaḥīn

title: The manager we've got
goal: Talk with Maryam about your internship: your job, the manager and the hours
tip: Talking about work with illi: il-mudīr illi ʿindana 'the manager we've got', il-muwaẓẓafīn illi wiyyāna 'the people who work with us'. Endings make work words personal: shughli 'my job', mudīri 'my manager', mashrūʿich 'your project' (to a woman).
dialogue: A
هلا! كيف الشغل ويانا؟
hala! chēf ish-shughul wiyyāna?
Hi! How's work with us going?
B
هلا فيج! زين، شغلي وايد حلو. والمدير اللي عندنا طيب
hala fīch! zēn, shughli wāyid ḥilu. w il-mudīr illi ʿindana ṭayyib
Hi! Good, I really like my job. And the manager we've got is nice.
A
هيه، والموظفين اللي ويانا كلهم طيبين
hē, w il-muwaẓẓafīn illi wiyyāna killhum ṭayybīn
Yes, and the people who work with us are all nice.
B
بس الدوام اللي عندنا يبدا الساعة سبع، بدري شوي!
bas id-dawām illi ʿindana yibda s-sāʿa sabʿ, badri shwayy!
But our working day starts at seven, that's a bit early!
A
صح. وأنا اليوم عندي اجتماع لين خمس
ṣaḥḥ. w ana l-yōm ʿindi ijtimāʿ lēn khams
True. And today I've got a meeting until five.
B
الاجتماع اللي عن مشروعج؟
il-ijtimāʿ illi ʿan mashrūʿich?
The one about your project?
A
هيه. أول ما أخلص، نشرب قهوة كلنا في المكتب
hē. awwal ma akhalliṣ, nishrab gahwa killna fi l-maktab
Yes. As soon as I finish, we'll all have a coffee in the office.
items: it starts, it begins (a masculine thing: the working day, the film)
(the one) we've got, at our place

title: I'm the one who sent it
goal: Tell Sēf about a mistake at work: what happened and who did it
tip: After a pronoun or a question word, illi gives 'the one who': ana illi ṭarrashtah 'I'm the one who sent it', minu illi…? 'who is it that…?'. ish-shay illi is 'the thing that': ish-shay illi kān fīh 'what was in it'. illi ṣār is 'what happened'.
grammar: ana illi, minu illi, ish-shay illi: 'the one who'
dialogue: A
شو فيه؟ شو اللي صار اليوم؟
shu fīh? shu illi ṣār il-yōm?
What's up? What happened today?
B
الإيميل اللي كان حق المدير، راح لكل اللي في الشركة!
il-īmēl illi kān ḥagg il-mudīr, rāḥ l-kill illi fi sh-sharika!
The email that was meant for the manager went to everyone in the company!
A
لا! ومنو اللي طرشه؟
la! w minu illi ṭarrashah?
No! And who sent it?
B
أنا اللي طرشته! ما دريت
ana illi ṭarrashtah! ma dirēt
I'm the one who sent it! I didn't realise.
A
والشي اللي كان فيه؟ مشكلة؟
w ish-shay illi kān fīh? mushkila?
And what was in it? Is it a problem?
B
لا، والمدير قال: اللي صار صار
la, w il-mudīr gāl: illi ṣār ṣār
No, and the manager said: what's done is done.
A
الحمد لله! مديرك ريّال زين
il-ḥamdu lillāh! mudīrak rayyāl zēn
Thank God! Your manager's a good guy.
items: I'm the one who, it was me who
I didn't realise, I didn't know
what's done is done (lit. what happened happened)
a good guy, a decent man
